test.title: Part 1–4: Cambridge IELTS 19 Academic Listening Test 4

items.quote: It's Kaeden.
items.prompt: Name of supervisor: ____

explanation.en: The supervisor corrects “Aiden” to Kaeden and spells K-A-E-D-E-N; the first guessed name is wrong.
explanation.kk: Жетекші Aiden атауын Kaeden деп түзетіп, K-A-E-D-E-N деп айтады; бастапқы болжам қате.
explanation.ru: Начальник исправляет Aiden на Kaeden и диктует K-A-E-D-E-N; первая догадка неверна.

items.quote: Put your coat and rucksack in one of the lockers there.
items.prompt: Where to leave coat and bag: use ____ in staffroom

explanation.en: Coat and rucksack go in the lockers in the staffroom; the key is for the locker, not the storage place itself.
explanation.kk: Күрте мен рюкзак қызметкерлер бөлмесіндегі lockers ішіне қойылады; кілт — сақтау орны емес.
explanation.ru: Куртку и рюкзак кладут в lockers в комнате персонала; ключ открывает шкафчик, но не является местом хранения.

items.quote: I was told to bring my passport with me.
items.prompt: See Tiffany in HR: to give ____ number

explanation.en: HR needs Charlotte’s passport number; an ID card is an alternative she does not have.
explanation.kk: Кадр бөліміне Шарлоттаның passport нөмірі керек; жеке куәлік — онда жоқ балама.
explanation.ru: Отделу кадров нужен номер passport Шарлотты; удостоверение — альтернатива, которой у неё нет.

items.quote: Tiffany will give you a uniform.
items.prompt: See Tiffany in HR: to collect ____

explanation.en: Tiffany supplies a uniform in the required size; the badge is collected separately at the front desk.
explanation.kk: Тиффани қажетті өлшемдегі uniform береді; бейдж бөлек қабылдау орнынан алынады.
explanation.ru: Тиффани выдаёт uniform нужного размера; бейдж получают отдельно у стойки.

items.quote: The staffroom's on the first floor, and HR are a couple of floors above that, on the third floor.
items.prompt: Location of HR office: on ____ floor

explanation.en: HR is on the third floor; the first floor is the staffroom, not HR.
explanation.kk: Кадр бөлімі third қабатта; first қызметкерлер бөлмесіне қатысты.
explanation.ru: Отдел кадров на third этаже; first относится к комнате персонала.

items.quote: It's oh-four-one-two double-six-five nine-oh-three.
items.prompt: Supervisor’s mobile number: ____

explanation.en: “Oh-four-one-two double-six-five nine-oh-three” gives 0412 665 903; “double-six” supplies two sixes.
explanation.kk: Oh-four-one-two double-six-five nine-oh-three — 0412 665 903; double-six екі алтыны білдіреді.
explanation.ru: Oh-four-one-two double-six-five nine-oh-three означает 0412 665 903; double-six — две шестёрки.

groups.title: First day at work
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

items.quote: When something needs a new price label, put a yellow one on the package, next to the original price.
items.prompt: Bakery section: use ____ labels

explanation.en: New price labels must be yellow and placed beside the original price; the gap asks for the colour.
explanation.kk: Жаңа баға белгісі yellow болып, ескі бағаның жанына қойылады; түсі сұралады.
explanation.ru: Новые ценники должны быть yellow рядом со старой ценой; нужен цвет.

items.quote: Beneath those is where we keep the plastic boxes — we run out of those really quickly, so you should bring more from the storeroom.
items.prompt: Sushi takeaway counter: re-stock with ____ boxes if needed

explanation.en: Restock plastic boxes from the storeroom; cardboard boxes are mentioned first but are not the ones running out.
explanation.kk: Қоймадан plastic қораптар толықтырылады; cardboard алдымен аталады, бірақ таусылатын олар емес.
explanation.ru: Пополняют plastic коробки со склада; cardboard упомянуто первым, но заканчиваются не они.

items.quote: The fish is laid on ice, but when that starts to melt, you'll need to get more from the cold-room.
items.prompt: Meat and fish counters: collect ____ for the fish from the cold-room

explanation.en: Fish is displayed on ice, which needs replacing when it melts; the scale is part of the cleaning task.
explanation.kk: Балық ice үстінде тұрады, ерігенде оны ауыстыру керек; таразы тазалау жұмысына қатысты.
explanation.ru: Рыба лежит на ice, который заменяют при таянии; весы относятся к уборке.

items.quote: But make sure you put on thermal gloves when you take anything out of the cold-room.
items.prompt: Meat and fish counters: must wear special ____

explanation.en: Thermal gloves are required in the cold-room; Charlotte does not need a hat because she will not serve customers.
explanation.kk: Суық бөлмеде gloves керек; Шарлотта сатып алушыға қызмет көрсетпегендіктен бас киім қажет емес.
explanation.ru: В холодильной комнате нужны gloves; шапка не нужна, поскольку Шарлотта не обслуживает покупателей.

items.quote: However, they don't work for everyone — especially if you suffer from something like a heart condition or asthma, because they're aimed at people with average fitness and running ability.
items.prompt: Which TWO problems with some training programmes for new runners does Liz mention?

options.text: There is a risk of serious injury.
They are unsuitable for certain age groups.
They are unsuitable for people with health issues.
It is difficult to stay motivated.
There is a lack of individual support.

explanation.en: They can be unsuitable for health conditions and lack individual answers; people of all ages use them.
explanation.kk: Бағдарлама ауруы бар адамға сәйкес емес және жеке сұраққа жауап бермейді; түрлі жасқа арналған.
explanation.ru: Программы не подходят при заболеваниях и не дают индивидуальных ответов; они рассчитаны на разные возраста.

items.quote: Listening to music can be very helpful — it takes your mind off things and helps your body get into rhythm.
items.prompt: Which TWO tips does Liz recommend for new runners?

options.text: going on runs with a friend

explanation.en: She recommends music and running twice weekly; she discourages running with a friend or very slowly.
explanation.kk: Кеңес — музыка және аптасына екі рет жүгіру; досымен не өте баяу жүгіру ұсынылмайды.
explanation.ru: Советы — музыка и два занятия в неделю; бег с другом и очень медленный темп не рекомендуются.

items.quote: She was worried about being left behind and being the slowest runner.
items.prompt: Ceri

explanation.en: She liked running but feared being left behind, showing a lack of confidence.
explanation.kk: Ол жүгіруді ұнатқан, бірақ артта қалудан қорыққан; себеп — сенімсіздік.
explanation.ru: Она любила бег, но боялась отстать; причина — неуверенность.

items.quote: James had always hated the idea of running but a friend encouraged him to come along for a taster session and he hasn't looked back.
items.prompt: James

explanation.en: He hated the idea of running; his busy job does not stop him now.
explanation.kk: Ол жүгіру идеясын жек көрген; жұмысы қазір кедергі емес.
explanation.ru: Он ненавидел идею бега; занятая работа не мешает ему теперь.

items.quote: Leo was worried about having to commit himself to training sessions every week and wasn't sure he'd be able to fit training into his busy schedule.
items.prompt: Leo

explanation.en: Leo doubted he could fit training into his busy schedule.
explanation.kk: Лео тығыз кестесінен уақыт табарына күмәнданған.
explanation.ru: Лео сомневался, что найдёт время в плотном графике.

items.quote: It took him months to find the courage to contact us but felt reassured immediately as there were other people his age who were only just taking up running for the first time.
items.prompt: Mark

explanation.en: He took months to find the courage to contact the club, showing low confidence rather than lack of time.
explanation.kk: Ол хабарласуға бірнеше ай батылдық жинаған — уақыт жетіспеуі емес, сенімсіздік.
explanation.ru: Он несколько месяцев набирался смелости позвонить — неуверенность, а не нехватка времени.

groups.title: Liz’s experience and race advice
groups.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

parts.context: A running coach gives advice and describes club members’ experiences.

transcript.text: My name's Liz Fuller and I'm a running coach with Compton Park Runners Club.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: Welcome to my podcast.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: If you're thinking about taking up running — I'm here to help.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: There are many training programmes available online which aim to help people build up to running 5 kilometres.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: Some of them are great and thousands of people of all ages are taking part in 5-kilometre races across the country as a result.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: People like them because they're easy to follow and don't push them too hard.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: However, they don't work for everyone — especially if you suffer from something like a heart condition or asthma, because they're aimed at people with average fitness and running ability.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: Another thing is that everyone is different — and if you have any specific questions related to your needs. there's no one to provide any answers.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: I have a couple of simple tips I always give to new runners.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: I expect you've been told to run very slowly until your fitness increases — well, I find that can prevent progress.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: You should run at a speed that feels comfortable, but time yourself and try to run a bit faster each time.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: Listening to music can be very helpful — it takes your mind off things and helps your body get into rhythm.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: I'd say that is better than running with a friend — especially as most people are competitive and that's not what you want when you're just starting.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: I don't think the time of day is especially important — some people are better in the evening, while others are morning people — but you need to be consistent, so aim to train regularly — twice a week is enough to begin with.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: New members often say to me that they've been put off running either because they lack confidence, or they don't have time, or they think they dislike running.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: Ceri, for example, joined the club two years ago at the age of 40.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: She'd always enjoyed running at school but wasn't sure if she'd be able to do it.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: She was worried about being left behind and being the slowest runner.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: But she says she was made to feel so welcome she soon forgot all about that.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: James had always hated the idea of running but a friend encouraged him to come along for a taster session and he hasn't looked back.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: He never misses a training session despite having a really demanding job.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: Leo was worried about having to commit himself to training sessions every week and wasn't sure he'd be able to fit training into his busy schedule.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: But after experiencing a lot of stress at work he came along to us and gave it a go.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: Now he says he feels much more relaxed and he looks forward to his weekly run.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: Mark is quite typical of our new members.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: He's never considered himself to be a sporty person and it was only when he retired that he decided to take up the challenge of trying to run 5 kilometres.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: It took him months to find the courage to contact us but felt reassured immediately as there were other people his age who were only just taking up running for the first time.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: My own journey hasn't been easy I did my first marathon when I was 37, after having had two kids.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: My husband had been running marathons for years, but I never dreamed I'd be doing one with him.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: I managed to complete it in four hours, but I felt like giving up halfway through — it was only the support of the spectators that kept me going.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: I do think signing up for a race of whatever length is motivating — whether it's 5K or 25K — because it's good to have something to work towards and it gives you a sense of achievement.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: I did my first 10K after only six months, which was certainly very challenging and not something I'd necessarily recommend.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: But after you've been training for a few weeks, it's worth putting your name down for a 5K — some people find they only need a few practice runs before taking part in a race, but I'd give yourself a couple of months at least.
transcript.speaker: LIZ

transcript.text: Well, I hope that's given
transcript.speaker: LIZ

items.prompt: Jane and Kieran agree that hardback books should be

explanation.ru: Они ценят книги на виду и красивые обложки; не предлагают дарить их посетителям.

items.quote: He watched me pull a heavy book off the shelf when I was small, and it fell on the floor and broke apart.
items.prompt: While talking about taking a book from a shelf, Jane

options.text: describes the mistakes other people make doing it.
reflects on a significant childhood experience.

parts.context: Two students discuss caring for books and the layout of a bookshop.

transcript.text: So Jane — you'll be off to Denmark soon to do your work placement.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: Yes, I'm really looking forward to it and I've just started packing up all my books to put in storage.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Well, I hope they don't get spoilt.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: It's OK — my grandfather works in a bookshop and he told me how to pack them.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Oh, that's helpful.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: He says you have to support the spine otherwise the paper can come away from the cover.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Yeah — that's obvious.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: He also told me to pack them flat in the box not on their side — again because they can bend and if you leave them like that for, say. a year. it's quite hard to get them back to their normal shape.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Well, it's pretty clear that ruins them, but a lot of people just can't be bothered to protect their books.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: He always says it's such a shame that publishers don't use better-quality paper.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: It's the acid in the paper that causes the problem, isn't it?
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: Yeah — that's why old books go yellow.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: You know some of the books my grandfather's given me are like that already.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Oh ...
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: I should dump them really if they're going to deteriorate further, but I'd feel bad.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: They'll always remind me of him.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: He's quite a collector, you know.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Well, if they're important to you ...
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: Yeah — I'd regret just throwing them away.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: You know, maybe it's because I was taught to treasure books ... but I hate seeing students force open the pages — of paperbacks.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: They press so hard they end up breaking the spine.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: I know, but unfortunately, paperbacks aren't designed to last a long time and people know that.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Hardbacks aren't quite as weak.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Yeah, they're different, I suppose.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: But I still don't think people value hardbacks like they used to.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: Well, they aren't decorative, are they, like other objects.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Plus, nowadays, people don't keep them out on shelves as much as they used to.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: That's such a pity.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: When I visit someone — if they have, say, a colourful book on a table, it's the first thing I'm drawn to.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: I agree — and book covers can be a work of art in themselves.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Some are really eye-catching.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: I've always been taught to handle books carefully.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: If you watch someone take a book off a shelf, well, they usually do it wrong.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: Ah, my grandfather says, you should put your hand right over the top of the book or if you can't do that, pull the other books on the shelf aside so that you can hold the whole cover.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: When did you learn all this?
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: He watched me pull a heavy book off the shelf when I was small, and it fell on the floor and broke apart.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Oh dear!
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: I can still remember it!
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: You know what I really like?
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: What?
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: The smell of new books.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: Me too.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: My parents used to laugh at me when I was a kid because I loved putting books up to my nose.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: Almost as much as reading them!
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: New books aren't cheap, though, are they?
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: I guess we're lucky we can buy them.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: My grandfather stocks second-hand books as well as new ones and they don't smell quite as good.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: I'd love to have a bookshop like your grandfather.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: What's it like?
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: Well, it's quite big — it's got two floors and an attic, and he stocks all kinds of books really.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: I guess he treasures things like first editions and other rare books.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: Yeah — you might think he'd keep those in the attic or somewhere.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: ... so they'd be hidden?
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: Yeah.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: But he likes people to know that he has them.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: So, he puts them out in the shop but makes sure you need a ladder to get them.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Right.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: That would prevent any thefts!
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: Uhuh.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Does he stock books for children?
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: He does.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: He particularly likes to encourage kids to read; he always says that he used to sit under the stairs as a child with a pile of books and read them all.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Oh cool.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: And then there's a place for pushchairs by the front door.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: And a café if anyone needs refreshments.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: That's good to know.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: As I said, it's a big shop and there's a storage area out the back as well.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Oh, what does he keep there?
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: Books he wants to throw away?
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: He hardly ever throws anything away — he just leaves unwanted books by the front door for customers to take.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Well, that's very nice.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: Yeah — and books people or institutions have requested, they all go at the far end.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Oh.
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: He thinks it's best to keep these out of the main shopping area as they're boxed and new.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: Did you get your coursebooks from him?
transcript.speaker: KIERAN

transcript.text: Naturally.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.text: He used to keep these books on the first floor, but now there's a new university in my hometown, he's moved them downstairs to attract the students.
transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.speaker: JANE

transcript.speaker: KIERAN

items.quote: Invasive species are a significant contributor to the current global biodiversity crisis and are often in competition with native species and may threaten their long-term survival.
items.prompt: Do not include invasive species because of possible ____ with native species.

explanation.en: Invasive species compete with native species; the notes require the noun “competition”.
explanation.kk: Инвазиялық түр жергілікті түрмен бәсекелеседі; жазбаға competition зат есімі қажет.
explanation.ru: Инвазивные виды конкурируют с местными; в заметках нужно существительное competition.

items.quote: These could include selecting trees that can contribute to wildlife conservation, improve the availability of food for the local community and maintain the stability of soil systems.
items.prompt: Aim to capture carbon, protect the environment and provide sustainable sources of ____ for local people.

explanation.en: A project can improve the availability of food for local people; wildlife and soil stability are other goals.
explanation.kk: Жоба жергілікті халыққа food қолжетімділігін арттырады; жануар мен топырақты қорғау — басқа мақсат.
explanation.ru: Проект обеспечивает местных жителей food; охрана животных и устойчивость почвы — другие цели.

items.quote: Using seeds with low genetic diversity generally lowers the resilience of restored forests, which can make them vulnerable to disease and unable to adapt to climate change.
items.prompt: Use tree seeds with a high genetic diversity to increase resistance to ____ and climate change.

explanation.en: Low genetic diversity makes forests vulnerable to disease; high diversity therefore improves resistance.
explanation.kk: Генетикалық әртүрлілік аз болса, орман disease алдында әлсіз; жоғары болса, төзімділігі артады.
explanation.ru: Низкое генетическое разнообразие повышает уязвимость к disease; высокое повышает устойчивость.

items.quote: Reforesting areas which are currently exploited for agriculture should be avoided as this often leads to other areas being deforested.
items.prompt: Plant trees on previously forested land which is in a bad condition, not land which is being used for ____.

explanation.en: Land currently used for agriculture should be avoided because this may cause deforestation elsewhere.
explanation.kk: Agriculture үшін қолданылатын жер алынбайды, өйткені бұл басқа жерде орман кесуге әкелуі мүмкін.
explanation.ru: Не выбирают землю, используемую для agriculture, поскольку это может вызвать вырубку в другом месте.

groups.title: Tree planting — reforestation principles
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

items.quote: Having detailed and up-to-date maps identifying high-priority areas for intervention is essential.
items.prompt: Base planning decisions on information from accurate ____.

explanation.en: Detailed, up-to-date maps identify priority areas; drones are a tool for collecting and monitoring information.
explanation.kk: Толық әрі жаңа maps басым жерді анықтайды; дрон — дерек жинау және бақылау құралы.
explanation.ru: Подробные современные maps определяют приоритетные участки; дроны — инструмент сбора и контроля данных.

items.quote: In Brazil, it's being used to identify and quantify how parts of the Amazon are being devastated by human activities such as rearing cattle and illegal logging.
items.prompt: Drones identify areas in Brazil endangered by keeping ____ and illegal logging.

explanation.en: Rearing cattle is identified as a damaging human activity in the Amazon, alongside illegal logging.
explanation.kk: Амазондағы cattle өсіру заңсыз ағаш кесумен бірге зиянды әрекет ретінде аталады.
explanation.ru: Разведение cattle названо вредной деятельностью в Амазонии наряду с незаконной вырубкой.

items.quote: They are central to tropical reforestation projects as they accelerate the speed of the recovery process by attracting animals and birds which act as natural seed dispersers.
items.prompt: Native fig trees increase the ____ of recovery by attracting animals and birds.

explanation.en: Fig trees accelerate the speed of forest recovery by attracting seed-dispersing animals and birds.
explanation.kk: Інжір тұқым тарататын жануар мен құсты тартып, орман қалпына келуінің speed қарқынын арттырады.
explanation.ru: Инжир ускоряет speed восстановления леса, привлекая животных и птиц, рассеивающих семена.

items.quote: At this site, for example, after only three rainy seasons, monkeys started visiting to eat the fig fruits, naturally dispersing seeds through defecation.
items.prompt: For example, ____ were soon attracted to the area.

explanation.en: Monkeys began visiting after three rainy seasons to eat figs and disperse seeds; birds are mentioned more generally.
explanation.kk: Үш жаңбыр маусымынан кейін monkeys жеміс жеп, тұқым таратуға келген; құстар жалпылама аталған.
explanation.ru: После трёх сезонов дождей пришли monkeys есть плоды и распространять семена; птицы упоминаются в общем.

groups.title: Large-scale projects and Lampang Province, Northern Thailand
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

items.quote: Destruction of the mangrove forests had a terrible impact on plant and animal life, and also badly affected the fishing industry, which was a major source of employment for local people living in coastal areas.
items.prompt: Destruction of mangrove forests made it difficult for people to make a living from ____.

explanation.en: Mangrove destruction harmed the fishing industry, a major source of employment for coastal residents.
explanation.kk: Мангр жойылуы жағалау халқының негізгі жұмысы fishing саласына зиян келтірген.
explanation.ru: Уничтожение мангров навредило fishing — главному источнику работы прибрежных жителей.

items.quote: The mangroves also act as a defence against the increased threat of flooding caused by climate change.
items.prompt: The mangrove reforestation project protects against the higher risk of ____.

explanation.en: Mangroves defend against the increased threat of flooding caused by climate change.
explanation.kk: Мангр климат өзгерісінен артқан flooding қаупінен қорғайды.
explanation.ru: Мангры защищают от возросшей из-за изменения климата угрозы flooding.

groups.title: Involving local communities — Madagascar
groups.instruction: Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

parts.context: A lecture considers responsible tree planting and reforestation projects.

transcript.text: Tree planting now dominates political and popular agendas and is often presented as an easy answer to the climate crisis, as well as a way for business corporations to offset their carbon emissions.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: But unfortunately, tree planting isn't as straightforward as some people think.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: When the wrong trees are planted in the wrong place, it can do considerably more damage than good, failing to help either people or the environment.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Reforestation projects are currently being undertaken on a huge scale in many countries and it's crucial that the right trees are selected.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: A mix of species should always be planted, typical of the local natural forest ecosystem and including rare and endangered species in order to create a rich ecosystem.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: It's important to avoid non-native species that could become invasive.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Invasive species are a significant contributor to the current global biodiversity crisis and are often in competition with native species and may threaten their long-term survival.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Restoring biodiversity that will maximise carbon capture is key when reforesting an area, but ideally any reforestation project should have several goals.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: These could include selecting trees that can contribute to wildlife conservation, improve the availability of food for the local community and maintain the stability of soil systems.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Meeting as many of these goals as possible, whilst doing no harm to local communities, native ecosystems and vulnerable species, is the sign of a highly successful tree-planting scheme.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: To ensure the survival and resilience of a planted forest, it's vital to use tree seeds with appropriate levels of genetic diversity: the amount of genetic variation found within a species is essential for their survival.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Using seeds with low genetic diversity generally lowers the resilience of restored forests, which can make them vulnerable to disease and unable to adapt to climate change.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Choosing the right location for reforestation projects is as important as choosing the right trees.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Ultimately, the best area for planting trees would be in formerly forested areas that are in poor condition.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: It's better to avoid non-forested landscapes such as natural grasslands, savannas or wetlands as these ecosystems already contribute greatly to capturing carbon.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: It would also be advantageous to choose an area where trees could provide other benefits, such as recreational spaces.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Reforesting areas which are currently exploited for agriculture should be avoided as this often leads to other areas being deforested.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Large-scale reforestation projects require careful planning.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Making the right decisions about where to plant trees depends on having the right information.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Having detailed and up-to-date maps identifying high-priority areas for intervention is essential.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Drone technology is a useful tool in helping to prioritise and monitor areas of degraded forest for restoration.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: In Brazil, it's being used to identify and quantify how parts of the Amazon are being devastated by human activities such as rearing cattle and illegal logging.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: A good example of where the right trees were picked to achieve a restored forest is in Lampang Province in Northern Thailand.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: A previously forested site which had been degraded through mining was reforested by a cement company together with Chiang Mai University.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: After spreading 60 cm of topsoil, they planted 14 different native tree species which included several species of fig.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Figs are a keystone species because of the critical role they play in maintaining wildlife populations.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: They are central to tropical reforestation projects as they accelerate the speed of the recovery process by attracting animals and birds which act as natural seed dispersers.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: This helps to promote diversity through the healthy regrowth of a wide range of plant species.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Unlike the majority of fruit trees, figs bear fruit all year round, providing a reliable food source for many species.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: At this site, for example, after only three rainy seasons, monkeys started visiting to eat the fig fruits, naturally dispersing seeds through defecation.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Reforestation projects should always aim to make sure that local communities are consulted and involved in the decision-making process.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The restoration of mangrove forests in Madagascar is an example of a project which has succeeded in creating real benefits for the community.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Destruction of the mangrove forests had a terrible impact on plant and animal life, and also badly affected the fishing industry, which was a major source of employment for local people living in coastal areas.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The reforestation project involved hiring local people to plant and care for the new mangrove trees.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: Millions of mangrove trees have now been planted which has resulted in the return of a healthy aquatic ecosystem.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: The mangroves also act as a defence against the increased threat of flooding caused by climate change.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: What's more, the local economy is more stable and thousands more Madagascans are now able to send their children to school.
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER

transcript.text: One other important point to consider .
transcript.speaker: SPEAKER
